4.1   Atomic targets
P05.1 (T3): Polyhedral regularity, with coeﬃcient conventions ﬁxed
Characterize balanced rational polyhedral pairs (X, γ) for which the BMPS envelope regular-
ity property holds. Treat the literal integral-slope/rational-constant class and its explicit real
scalar extension separately. Literal regularity is classiﬁed in dimension one and fails on ev-
ery noncompact ﬁnite rational polyhedral space; the compact higher-dimensional literal case,
higher-dimensional real-PA case, and arbitrary nonseparable obstacles remain.

P05.5 (T4): Global polarized realization of polyhedral measures
Characterize polarized Monge–Ampère realizations of (X, γ). Construct global semipositive
lifts of the relative potentials ai − γ in a named BFJ domain, prove intersection-mass and
component-calibration identities, and compare global non-Archimedean and polyhedral mea-
sures, including mixed products and boundary terms. Local recursive CLD/delta comparison
is an established subcase, not the full target.

4.2   What constitutes a solution
Fix the PA coeﬃcient convention before stating regularity. Orthogonality requires the contact
integral, not just total mass. A global BFJ comparison must name the polarization, operator
domain, lifts, saturated lattice indices, intersection normalization and boundary terms; the
already resolved local recursive comparisons are not new atoms.

4.3   Full statement and detailed state of the art
Problem 4.1. Let X be a pure-dimensional balanced rational polyhedral space and let γ be
a piecewise-aﬃne polyhedrally convex reference function positive at inﬁnity. Characterize the
pairs (X, γ) for which the regularity and orthogonality properties of Botero–Mazzon–Pille-
Schneider hold. Under realizability hypotheses, compare their polyhedral Monge–Ampère
operator with CLD, delta-form, and non-Archimedean Monge–Ampère measures.

    The source itself formulates three sharper tasks that organize this broad problem: enlarge
the notion of polyhedral smoothness so that higher-dimensional regularity and orthogonality
hold; characterize polarized Calabi–Yau families whose tropicalizations satisfy those proper-
ties; and determine which matroids have Bergman fans satisfying orthogonality [BMPS26,
pp. 3–5, §1.5, and Remark 6.27]. By contrast, the analytic realization of the cross-fan was
a diagnostic problem formulated in this book, not a question attributed to Botero–Mazzon–
Pille–Schneider. Its literal compact-source and weighted-current parts are now settled by
Book Proposition 69.2.3, Book Proposition 69.2.4. The source’s only stronger strict-positivity
prospect is expressly assigned to its upcoming sequel: its bibliography lists that sequel as “in
preparation.” It is therefore not used here as an available theorem on regularity or orthog-
onality [BMPS26, pp. 5 and 60]. The stronger upstairs-equality problem in Problem 12.1
is not merely book-local: after removing an ill-deﬁned delta-current alternative, it is pre-
cisely the analytic specialization of the Bedford–Taylor question posed in [CLD25, §8.6.1 and
Deﬁnition 8.6.2].
    Thus the audit gives six verdicts. The real-scalar complete aﬃne case in Theorem 4.22
is veriﬁed, whereas literal integral-slope regularity already fails on the aﬃne line by Proposi-
tion 4.2; strict positivity alone is disproved by Example 4.25; positive growth alone, even on
the displayed Bergman fan, cannot force the conjunction of regularity and orthogonality by
Proposition 4.26; the recursive CLD and delta-form comparison is veriﬁed under the intrinsic
proper calibration hypotheses of Proposition 4.27, with the genuine algebraic tropicalization
supplied, under its stated value-group hypothesis, by Corollary 4.28; the global polarized
non-Archimedean Monge–Ampère comparison remains open beyond the realized source cases
because the proper polarization, lift, mass, and component calibration are additional inputs;
and the main higher-dimensional local contact problem remains open. The missing local asser-
tion is a contact theorem on singular fans: under an intrinsic smoothness and strict-positivity
package, positive top intersection mass of an envelope should force contact with the obstacle.
Neither a proof nor a counterexample satisfying both parts of that package is presently known.
